content.comment_body: I want to connect a linear actuator to a [product_name] PLC system. I have a [product_name] analog module, another analog output module, a relay module, a power supply unit (24V/4A), and a 12V transformer. The actuator model is Glideforce GF23-120504-3-65 High-Speed LD. I believe it needs to be wired through the transformer, but I'm unsure. Any wiring diagram or advice would be appreciated. Thank you.

The actuator operates at 12V DC, so a dedicated 12V DC power supply is needed. The actuator also draws a significant current (7A). The relays in the [product_name] system offer only make contacts, not changeover contacts, so you will need to add coupling relays externally.
Hello [user_name], I've attached the wiring diagram.

Thank you for the diagram. If I want the actuator to operate through the PLC, it appears the PLC and actuator are just using separate power supplies. Would I need to interface it with the analog output module?

Is there confusion about the wiring diagram? The program in the [product_name] PLC controls the coupling relays K1 and K2, using their changeover contacts. Activating K1 (and not K2) drives the actuator backwards, while activating K2 (and not K1) drives it forwards.
I understand now, thank you for clarifying.
Including diodes is essential for protection. For example, you can use a diode type like 1N4007.
